decisionsTitle: The registrations list, worked without leaving it: the verbs pinned, the list fitting a wide screen, a row's press back on its row, the notes in a tooltip, invitations by state, telephones on demand (amending §322, §652, §661, §737, §777, §942)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-11-12**, with a picture of the registrations list on a 1858-px screen: «Bun, avem de făcut niște UI/UX boss, că e jale! Aici mi se face crop!» — the last column, «Acțiuni», cut at the frame's edge (a row's press reading «VEZI INVITAȚI», the «Coloane» button half out), an address broken a few characters to a line and eight lines to a row, the event's title seven lines down a narrow column, the same title on every row. And while it was being repaired: «Coloana de partener ar trebui să apară ultima».

**What was wrong, measured.** One cause. The list's twelve columns asked for 1896 px at their least, and the frame on that screen has 1808. §652 decided that a table wider than its frame scrolls inside it and never the page — and nothing on screen said so: the scrollbar is at the foot of a list several screens long, so the frame read as cut, not as scrollable. What fell outside was whatever stood last, and the last column of every backoffice table is the one a row is acted on by: its verbs, the bulk tick, and «Coloane» itself — the one control that could have made the table narrower. §942 met the same cut a day earlier at 1280 px and moved «Partener» from last to third so that it was not the cell cut; the verbs stayed cut, at every width under about 1950 px. The width itself went to things nobody reads: «Număr de concurs (BIB)», one line with its arrow and its «?», held 247 px over a column of two digits; five «?» of 44 px each; 32 px of side padding in each of twelve cells; and «Eveniment», which with one event chosen says the filter's own choice on every row. Meanwhile an address may break at any character (so a long one never widens the page), which is exactly why the browser's table layout counted that column as one character wide and squeezed it to its heading.

**Decision.** Three parts, the first two in `AdminTable`, so every backoffice list has them.

**1. The row verbs' column is pinned to the frame's right edge.** `position: sticky; right: 0` on the verbs' heading and on every row's verbs cell, a lead row's too (the cells are marked `data-pinned` and styled from the table). CSS alone, so it holds in the server's HTML, before hydration and with JavaScript off: a pinning decided by an island would draw the verbs outside the frame first and move them in a moment later. The other columns scroll under it; a row's verbs, the bulk tick and «Coloane» are never the cells a narrow frame cuts. A pinned cell has to be opaque, in the colour of what is behind the table — the page, or the card when the table stands in a `Panel` or a boxed fold — and a table cannot see which. So the card says it: one CSS variable, `--br-surface` (`shared/ui/surface.ts`, `ON_CARD_SX` beside the card's own `bgcolor` in `Panel` and in `BOXED_DISCLOSURE_SX`), read with the page's colour as its fallback; the row's own fill — the heading's, a lead row's, a hovered row's — is laid over it again as an image, so a pinned cell is the colour of the cells beside it in both schemes. It sits above the column edges (§652), which pass under it. While columns lie under it its left edge fades into them: the table's island (`ColumnWidths`) keeps `data-more-end` on the frame with the chips rows' own watcher (`watchScrollRow`, §720), true to the scroll, to a drag that widens the table and to a column hidden or shown; a table that fits wears no edge at all. The same island keeps the frame's `scroll-padding-right` as wide as the pinned column, so a press the browser scrolls into view — reached with Tab in the column beside the verbs — stops beside them and not under them (WCAG 2.4.11), as the page's own scroll padding does for the sticky header. In a resized table the verbs' cell no longer clips (its width is always the measured one, so its one line fits, and its fade lies outside it).

**2. A heading takes no more room than it needs.** In the automatic layout a heading longer than 7em wraps onto a second line rather than widening its column: a box as wide as its text and never wider than 7em — a definite width, so a table squeezed to its least cannot wrap it further, a word to a line. A resized table lets it go and wraps a heading to its column's own width, as §652 has it, and the pre-paint script says the same before hydration. Under a mouse (`pointer: fine`) a heading's «?» is its glyph and a small ring, 30 px, and a cell's side padding is 12 px; under a finger both keep what a thumb needs, 44 and 16, and so does the phone layout's line of hints. A column's edge under a mouse reaches 8 px into each cell, so it stays inside that padding.

**3. The registrations list asks for no width it does not use.** «Eveniment» is drawn only while every event is listed; with one event chosen — the list's default (§178) — no column repeats it, and the invitations drawn above the rows (§737), which stand only where one event is chosen, carry no cell for it. Where it is drawn its title stands on a floor of 12rem, so it is a few lines and never a word to a line. An address stands on a floor of 12rem too, from `lg`, where the column is drawn — a phone's card keeps its own width — so it reads on a line and still breaks anywhere when it is longer. And «Partener» is the last column, right before the row's verbs, amending §942: it stood third only while the frame cut whatever stood last, and nothing is cut now. The phone's card follows the same order.

**The result, measured in a browser.** One event's list asks for 1734 px at its least, so it fits whole from a window of about 1784 px: on the owner's 1858 px with 74 to spare, no sideways scroll, no fade. An invitation's row went from 181 px tall to 69. At 1280 px the table still scrolls — eleven columns do not fit a laptop — with the verbs in view and «Partener» at the frame's end. With every event listed the table asks for 1950 px and scrolls 142 px on that screen, under the pinned verbs.

**Refused.**
- **Pinning the name column as well.** A frozen first column is the natural pair, and on a 1024-px screen the two pinned columns would hold 390 px of a 974-px frame. Not asked; the verbs were what was lost.
- **Dropping more columns by breakpoint** so that the table always fits. A column a breakpoint hides is one the person cannot bring back at that width; which columns to give up is «Coloane»'s question (§661), and its button is always in view now.
- **Shortening «Număr de concurs (BIB)».** The words are the owner's (§173); the heading wraps instead.
- **Deciding the pinning in JavaScript**, only while the table overflows: no surface colour to know, and the verbs would jump into the frame at hydration on every page load.
- **A fade at the frame's left edge**, once scrolled: a mask on a scroller several screens tall, for a state the person has just made themselves.
- **A data grid.** §53's reasons stand; this is CSS in the table that exists.

**What does not change.** The phone layout has no columns and is untouched. The exports keep their own columns, «Eveniment» included. The stored widths and hidden columns keep their keys; `?sort=event` is still a sort the list accepts. No migration, no dependency, no word changed.

**Tested.** `tests/unit/staff/admin-table-pinned-verbs.test.ts`: the marks on the verbs' heading and on every row's verbs, none on a table without verbs; the pinning's own CSS (sticky, the right edge, above the column edges, the surface's colour, the three fills); the fade only under the frame's `data-more-end`; the surface variable and the two cards that say it; the heading's box, the pre-paint script's release of it, and the mouse's sizes. `admin-table-column-widths.test.ts` reads the script's new rule in the style it writes. On PGlite (`tests/integration/registrations/partner-column.test.ts`): «Partener» last, after «Trimisă»; «Eveniment» absent with one event chosen and present, on its floor, with every event, nothing else moved; the address's floor on a row and on a lead row, and no event cell on a lead row. In a browser (`tests/e2e/admin-column-widths.spec.ts`, against a production build): at 1000 px the table is wider than its frame, the page does not scroll, the verbs' heading and a row's verbs are whole inside the frame, opaque, the edge faded; a press focused in the last column stops beside the verbs; at the frame's end the fade is gone and the last column stands whole beside them; at 1858 px the table fits, an address is one line and the long heading two. `tests/e2e/partner-mark.spec.ts` walks «Partener» as the last column at 1280 px, whole between the frame's edge and the verbs.

---

**The same day, the owner again**, six lines after the first repair: «Ar trebui să văd nota și pe tooltip, fără să deschid înscrierea» · «Mă disperă în general că atunci când fac un edit gen „aleg partenerul” și navighezi» · «trebuie să pot filtra și invitațiile după stare» · «Aș vrea să afișez și numărul de telefon al alergătorilor în grid ca să pot să-i sun rapid» · «și ar trebui să pot ascunde coloane să am un grid management». The last one exists since §661 — «Coloane», in the verbs' heading — and was the button the frame cut; pinned, it is in view at every width. The other four are below.

**4. A row's press comes back to its row, and the row stays where it was.** Every press on a row of the list answered at `#admin-alert`, the top of a page whose table starts several screens down — and half of them («Retrimite», «Anulează», «Confirmă pe hârtie», the check-in, the printing mark) did not come back to the list at all: they opened the registration's own page. Now every form of a row carries the list's own query (`listQuery`, in the one fragment all of a row's forms share), and the one return (`domain/list-row.ts#listReturnHref`: only the query travels, the path is rebuilt, the keys of an older outcome dropped) sends a press that went through to the row's own address, `#reg-<id>` — `AdminTable`'s `rowId`, as the shop's orders have had since §847 — with the outcome in the toast. A refusal still lands on the list's alert, where its sentence is, and a refused «Retrimite» pressed from the list now says so on the list. Pressed from the registration's page (no `listQuery`) every verb returns where it always did.

A fragment alone would still move the row: a browser answers one by putting its target at the top of the window, so the row under the hand jumped up the screen. One island (`KeepRowPlace`) undoes that: when a form naming a row and the list is sent it notes how far down the window the row stands — its row of the wide table, or on a phone the block that stands for it (`data-row-anchor`) — and when the list comes back on that row's address it scrolls by the difference, once, in the frame of the router's own scroll and before it is painted. It is handed one string and no row. With scripts off the fragment alone decides. Measured: a partner chosen on the twenty-first row, the row at 422 px before and at 422 px after; on a phone, a note saved from a card, the card at 349 px before and after while the alert above it took 48.

**5. The notes' words in the marker's tooltip.** §777 drew «2 note» on a row and kept the words for the registration's page. The marker now wears them: the three newest, each «<day and hour>: <words>» with the note's own lines, a long one cut at 280 characters, the older ones counted in the last line («… și încă 2 note»). No author is named — who wrote a note is the card's to say. Read in the one grouped query the list already made for the count (the export's reader), only for a role that may keep notes; the guard `notes-never-leave.test.ts` says so and still refuses the desk, the exports' writers, the public pages and every email. The marker stays the link to the card.

**6. «Stare» filters the invitations too.** The select gains, with one event chosen, the three states of an invitation not accepted yet, in the words their rows wear: «Invitație trimisă», «Invitație expirată», «Invitație retrasă» (`status=invitation-sent` and its two sisters, never mistakable for a registration's state, which is written in capitals). Chosen, the grid is that state's invitations and nothing else — a registration has no such state — on any page, and the search box then looks in the invitations' names and addresses. An accepted invitation is a registration and is found by its own state. With every event listed the three are not offered and the parameter says nothing. The export links are unchanged: they hand out registrations, and say nothing of invitations.

**7. «Arată telefoanele»: the telephones in the grid, on demand.** This one meets a rule. §322, after the GDPR audit, put the telephone with the emergency details: read by whoever may read the registrations, only when asked for, each read recorded, never on the desk and never in an export — and the list's own query was written to carry only *whether* a telephone is held. A column always drawn would read a hundred telephones on every page of the list with no trail. So the rule is kept and the grid gets its column: a plain link above the table, «Arată telefoanele» (`?phones=1`, kept while the list is sorted, paged and worked on), draws «Telefon» after the address — the number as typed, on one line, a `tel:` link — and each page drawn with it is recorded before the numbers come back, `registrations.phones_viewed`: who, the event when one is chosen, how many rows, never a number or a name; a page of no rows records nothing. Their own query (`findPhonesOf`), the role asserted in the service (`readRowPhones`, `canReadRegistrations`). It is not one of «Coloane»'s columns, because hiding there is a view and this is a read. The form already tells the person «Un organizator te poate suna în legătură cu evenimentul»; the emergency contact's name and number are not in the column and stay where §322 put them. With the column on, one event's list asks for about 1860 px and scrolls some 55 px on the owner's screen, under the pinned verbs.

**Refused, of the second part.**
- **The telephone always in the grid.** It would quietly reverse §322. If the club decides the trail is not worth the click, it is one decision to take knowingly, not a column to add.
- **Returning a result instead of redirecting**, so that nothing navigates at all. Every backoffice write redirects and says its outcome in the address (§384's toast rides on it, and so does every test of a press); changing that for a row's verbs is a change to all of them.
- **A fourth choice, «Invitație acceptată».** It would list registrations under an invitation's name.

**Tested, the second part.** `tests/unit/registrations/list-row.test.ts` (the row's address, the alert for a refusal or an id that is not one, the query rebuilt, a typed address going nowhere) and `tests/integration/registrations/row-press-returns.test.ts` (the real actions on PGlite: «Retrimite» from the list and from the page, a refused one, the check-in, the printing mark, the cancel). `tests/unit/shared/notes-tip.test.ts` and `registration-notes-screens.test.ts` (the tooltip's words on the page). `partner-column.test.ts`: every form of a row carries the query once and the table names its rows; the three invitation states, the search among them, every event listed; the telephones — no column and no read until asked, the link, one trail row with the count and no number, every role. In a browser (`tests/e2e/partner-mark.spec.ts`, 320 px and desktop): a partner saved from a row, the address the row's own, the row or its card within 3 px of where it was pressed.
changelogLine: - **The registrations list, worked without leaving it** — «Acțiuni» stays at the frame's right edge on every backoffice list, and one event's registrations fit a 1858-px screen whole («Eveniment» only with every event listed, an address on one line, «Partener» last). A press on a row — choosing a partner, a note, «Retrimite», «Anulează», the check-in — comes back to that row, which stays where it was on screen, with the outcome in the toast. The notes marker shows the notes' words in its tooltip. «Stare» also filters the event's invitations: sent, expired, withdrawn. «Arată telefoanele» adds a «Telefon» column with numbers to tap; each page shown with it is recorded. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given a backoffice list at `md` and up whose table is wider than its frame, then the row verbs' column — its heading with «Coloane», each row's verbs and each lead row's — stays whole inside the frame, at its right edge, without scrolling, by CSS alone (in the server's HTML, before hydration and with JavaScript off), opaque in the colour of the surface the table stands on (the page, or the card of a `Panel` or a boxed fold) under its row's own fill, the other columns passing under it and the page never scrolling sideways; with JavaScript on its edge fades into those columns only while more lies that way, and a control the browser scrolls into view stops beside it, not under it; in the automatic layout a heading longer than 7em wraps onto a second line rather than widening its column, a resized table wrapping it to its column's own width as criterion 193 has it; under a fine pointer a heading's «?» is 30 px and a cell's side padding 12 px, a coarse pointer keeping 44 and 16 (2026-11-12, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 22 in where the column stands. Given the registrations list at `md` and up, then «Partener» is the last column, right before the row's verbs; «Eveniment» is drawn only while every event is listed — with one event chosen no column and no invitation's row repeats it — its title on a floor of 12rem; an address stands on a floor of 12rem from `lg` (none in the phone's card), so it reads on a line and still breaks anywhere when longer; and with one event chosen the whole table fits its frame on a 1858-px screen, nothing scrolling sideways (2026-11-12, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a press on a row of the registrations list — the row's dialogs, «Retrimite», and every verb of its «⋮» — then the form carries the list's own query and never a path, and a press that went through returns to that list, as it stood, at the row's own address (`#reg-<id>`) with the outcome in the toast, while a refusal returns to the list's alert; the same verb pressed from the registration's page returns to that page; with JavaScript on the row, or on a phone the block that stands for it, is within a few pixels of where it stood when pressed (2026-11-12, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a registration with internal notes and a reader who may keep notes, then the list's notes marker shows in its tooltip the three newest notes' words, each with its day and hour and its own lines, a note over 280 characters cut, the older ones counted, and no author's name — read in one grouped query for the page; the marker is still the link to the notes card, and the notes are on no desk screen, public page or email (2026-11-12, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the registrations list with one event chosen, then «Stare» also offers «Invitație trimisă», «Invitație expirată» and «Invitație retrasă», and choosing one lists that state's invitations and no registration, on any page, the search box looking in their names and addresses; with every event listed the three are not offered and the parameter is ignored (2026-11-12, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the registrations list, then no telephone is read or drawn until the reader presses «Arată telefoanele»; pressed, a «Telefon» column follows the address with each number as typed on a `tel:` link («—» without one), the choice riding on every sort, page and row press until «Ascunde telefoanele», and each page drawn with it writes one audit row (`registrations.phones_viewed`: the reader, the event when one is chosen, the row count, never a number or a name) before the numbers are returned — none for a page of no rows; only a role that may read the registrations is answered, the service refusing every other with nothing recorded; the emergency contact's details are not in the column (2026-11-12, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the registrations list worked without leaving it: verbs pinned, a row's press back on its row, notes in a tooltip, invitations by state, telephones on demand
